- File: .github/workflows/nightly-validation-selftest.yml; scripts/validation_selftest_matrix.py
  Line or code reference: Workflow lines 43-52 run the self-test before lines 129-157 expose `STATUS_PUSH_TOKEN` and run `git pull` / `git push`. `validation_selftest_matrix.py:274-310` creates each fixture workspace beneath the checkout and runs the test driver there.
  Problem: A self-test can plant an executable `.git/hooks/pre-push` in the enclosing checkout. The later token-bearing push does not disable or isolate repository hooks.
  Why it fails at runtime: The fixture workspace has no `.git` of its own, so Git discovers the checkout’s `.git` directory above it. A test running as the same user can write there. During the later `git push`, Git runs the planted hook with `STATUS_PUSH_TOKEN` in its environment, allowing the test’s code to capture the write-capable token. `persist-credentials: false` prevents direct token access during tests but does not prevent them from arranging code to run when the token is introduced later.
  SEVERITY: BLOCKER
